title: Publish deployment boundaries and independent service bootstrap
author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4

events.title: Publish deployment boundaries and independent service bootstrap
events.body:
## Outcome

Make every service boundary and failure mode machine-readable, then prove the network can run without the repository's default public deployment.

## Implementation

- Define a deployment manifest for canonical, cached, transient, encrypted, and observable data plus retention and operator ownership.
- Package independently configurable relay and control, public index and search, web, seed, identity resolution, room relay, workflow broker, and organization service roles.
- Provide one declarative bootstrap that can colocate roles or point each role at an independent operator.
- Add signed configuration export and import, health, backup boundaries, and conformance checks for every role.
- Document and test identity resolution, public discovery, cloning, contribution routing, and recovery when the default public services disappear.

## Acceptance criteria

- A clean self-host fixture starts every role without a hidden dependency on a default public endpoint.
- Removing the default control plane leaves existing repositories cloneable and independently discoverable.
- The manifest states exactly which metadata each role can and cannot observe.
- Canonical Git and collaboration data remain with configured repository nodes.
- Configuration migration rejects secret leakage, unknown roles, and incompatible schema versions.

## Dependencies

Builds on #442, #456, #473, and protocol schemas from #474.

## Verification

Start a full independent topology, import configuration, clone and contribute, remove each role and the default public endpoints in turn, restore it, and verify declared failure behavior and data boundaries.
